record.paper_title: Advances in periodic difference equations with open problems
record.original_question: In a p-periodic system [f0, …, f_{p-1}] of continuous interval maps, define A_{p,q} = {n : lcm(n, p) = q p}. Suppose some least period m of the system lies in A_{p,q}, where q > 1 is odd. Must the period p q also belong to Per([f0, …, f_{p-1}])? Prove that it must, or produce a counterexample.

evidence.quote: For q ∈ N, define the clusters Ap,q = {n : lcm(n, p) = q · p} = {n : q = n/gcd(n, p)}.
Open Problem 2.2. Suppose m ∈ Per([f0, ..., fp−1]) for some m ∈ Ap,q, where q > 1 is an odd number. Prove that pq ∈ Per([f0, ..., fp−1]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be a compact interval and let $f_0, f_1, \dots, f_{p-1} : I \to I$ be continuous maps. Consider the non-autonomous periodic difference equation
$$x_{n+1} = f_{n \bmod p}(x_n), \qquad n = 0, 1, 2, \dots,$$
and write $F = [f_0, \dots, f_{p-1}]$ for this $p$-periodic system. A point $x \in I$ is called a periodic point of $F$ of period $m$ if $m$ is the least positive integer such that $(f_{m-1} \circ \cdots \circ f_1 \circ f_0)(x) = x$ when iterating the system starting at index $0$, and more generally $m$ is a period of $F$ if some orbit of the system has minimal period $m$. Let $\mathrm{Per}(F)$ denote the set of all such minimal periods.

For $q \in \mathbb{N}$, define the cluster
$$A_{p,q} \;=\; \{\, n \in \mathbb{N} : \mathrm{lcm}(n, p) = q \cdot p \,\} \;=\; \{\, n \in \mathbb{N} : q = n / \gcd(n, p) \,\}.$$

Question: Suppose there exists $m \in \mathrm{Per}(F)$ with $m \in A_{p,q}$, where $q > 1$ is an odd integer. Must it follow that $pq \in \mathrm{Per}(F)$? Either prove that $pq \in \mathrm{Per}(F)$ in this situation for every such $p$-periodic system of continuous interval maps, or exhibit a $p$-periodic system $F$ and odd $q > 1$ for which $m \in A_{p,q} \cap \mathrm{Per}(F)$ but $pq \notin \mathrm{Per}(F)$.
artifact.category_tag: Periodic difference equations and Sharkovsky-type orderings
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as Open Problem 2.2 in a survey on advances in periodic difference equations. Related literature (AlSharawi–Angelos–Elaydi–Rakesh, and follow-ups on extensions of Sharkovsky's theorem to periodic difference equations) develops cluster-based Sharkovsky orderings but does not appear to settle this specific odd-cluster forcing question; no published resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: An extension of Sharkovsky's theorem to periodic difference equations
status_evidence.snippet: Extension of Sharkovsky's theorem and its converse to periodic difference equations; constructs p-periodic difference equations with prescribed geometric cycles.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational result on Sharkovsky-type ordering for p-periodic systems, but does not resolve the odd-cluster open problem.

status_evidence.title: Nonautonomous Difference Equations: Open Problems and Conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open problems in nonautonomous difference equations including period-set forcing questions.
status_evidence.claim: Lists related open questions, indicating the odd-cluster forcing problem remains open.
